added_models.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant

engagement.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
engagement.note: AZD8931 plus tamoxifen cut pHER2, pMAPK and pAKT in MCF7/TamRes tumours; MINT took no patient tumour PD readout.
engagement.short: Tumour pHER2/pAKT readout never taken in MINT
engagement.quote: Under ligand-stimulated conditions, AZD8931 more potently inhibited HER signaling than lapatinib or gefitinib.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4030601 author manuscript). Johnston 2016 abstract lists no pharmacodynamic endpoint.
engagement.judgement: The model's PD readout is tumour HER-pathway phosphorylation; no sapitinib trial reported one, so engagement stays untested on this track.

dose.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
dose.note: Mice got AZD8931 100 mg/kg daily by gavage with no exposure target or tolerability margin stated; MINT used 20 and 40 mg bid.
dose.short: No exposure target stated for mice
dose.quote: For studies in vivo, transplantable MCF7/TamRes xenografts were treated with tamoxifen or fulvestrant, either alone or in combination with AZD8931.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read: 100 mg/kg daily oral gavage; no plasma exposure, no body-weight or tolerability data reported.
dose.judgement: No exposure target or margin in the model paper, so neither the 'reached' rows nor decision 16 can be applied; mirrors the checker-confirmed call on the Hickinson 2010 track.

efficacy.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
efficacy.note: AZD8931 delayed MCF7/TamRes xenograft growth with tamoxifen or fulvestrant, without regression; minimal added benefit in endocrine-naive MCF7 cells.
efficacy.quote: AZD8931 also significantly delayed the growth of MCF7 TamRes xenografts in the presence of tamoxifen or fulvestrant.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use. The in-vivo prediction (benefit in tamoxifen-resistant ER+/HER2-negative disease) was never taken into a trial of endocrine-resistant patients.

efficacy.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
efficacy.note: Morrison 2014 cites MINT's null in endocrine-naive patients as expected from its data, which showed minimal benefit outside the tamoxifen-resistant setting.
efficacy.short: MINT null reconciled post hoc with model
efficacy.quote: In this trial, AZD8931 was combined with anastrozole in women with endocrine therapy-naive advanced breast cancer where growth factor signaling would be expected to be less and overall there was no evidence of significant therapeutic benefit.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. MINT was public as a 2013 ASCO abstract (Johnston, J Clin Oncol 2013, the paper's ref 46) before this paper; whether the xenograft experiments predate June 2013 is not stated.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: minimal added endocrine sensitivity in parental MCF7 (greater in T47D), growth delay only in TamRes xenografts; MINT PFS HR 1.37 and 1.16 vs placebo
efficacy.population: HR+ HER2-non-amplified, endocrine-naive advanced breast cancer (MINT); model: tamoxifen-resistant
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison, but made after MINT's result was reported (ASCO 2013), so decision 10 makes it a retrodiction: the paper's own naive-versus-resistant split reproduces the null (retro, partial: T47D parental cells had shown a greater effect). Read prospectively it would be same/partial; read as 'AZD8931 plus endocrine therapy helps ER+/HER2-negative disease' it would be the checker's contra. The xenograft prediction itself (endocrine-resistant patients) was never tested. Patient-level track, so it carries MINT's population rather than the context's HER2-positive one.
efficacy.reason: Model paper reconciles MINT null post hoc

patient_trials.quote: AZD8931, in combination with endocrine therapy, does not appear to enhance endocrine responsiveness and is associated with greater skin and gastrointestinal toxicity.

safety.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
safety.note: Mice dosed 100 mg/kg daily to 1000 mm3 endpoints; the paper reports no body weight, diarrhoea or other tolerability finding.
safety.quote: The strongest inhibition was achieved with a fulvestrant and AZD8931 combination, though no tumor regression was observed.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read: no tolerability, weight or toxicity statement anywhere in the manuscript.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: the model made no tolerability statement.

safety.model: ER+/HER2-negative tamoxifen-resistant MCF7 and T47D lines and MCF7/TamRes xenografts under tamoxifen or fulvestrant
safety.note: Mice can show EGFR-TKI diarrhoea and the model was silent; MINT: diarrhoea 40 and 51 % vs 12 %, rash 32 and 48 % vs 12 %.
safety.short: Silence on diarrhoea contradicted in MINT
safety.quote: Safety findings showed a greater incidence of diarrhea (40, 51, and 12 % for AZD8931 20, 40 mg, and placebo, respectively), rash (32, 48, and 12 %)
safety.confidence_note: Johnston 2016 abstract (paywalled); registry results posted 2014-05-08 set the year. Quote is a verbatim leading fragment of the abstract's safety sentence.
safety.population: HR+ HER2-non-amplified, endocrine-naive advanced breast cancer (MINT)
safety.judgement: Same rule the checker applied to the Hickinson 2010 track: a mouse dosed daily for weeks could have shown diarrhoea or weight loss, the paper reports neither, and MINT's diarrhoea and rash are the class harm. Sibling population transfers for safety (decision 12).
safety.reason: Mouse silent on class GI/skin harm

considered_not_added: Ba/F3 ERBB2-mutant TKI panel with PDX (Robichaux 2019 Cancer Cell, 10.1016/j.ccell.2019.09.001, poziotinib most potent mutant-selective TKI): the only patient comparison is HER2 exon 20 NSCLC (ORR 42 %), cross-indication; the breast-side trials have no result (NCT04172597 cohort 1, HER2-mutant breast cancer, results posted 2024-03-13 with no ORR for that cohort; NCT02544997 HER2/EGFR-mutant MBC completed 2020-02, no results, no publication).
Pyrotinib in HER2-non-amplified HER2-mutant breast cancer (NCT03412383): status unknown, no results, no publication and no breast-specific model paper found, so no comparison.

Pyrotinib PBPK CYP3A4 drug-interaction model (Adv Ther 2023, 10.1007/s12325-023-02602-1): in-silico model fitted to clinical single-dose PK, then compared with observed itraconazole and rifampicin DDI (rifampicin underestimated); a co-medication exposure model built on patient PK, not a preclinical dose-selection prediction, and retrodictive; abstract only.

Patient-derived organoids or PDX co-clinical use for pyrotinib or poziotinib in breast cancer: Europe PMC searches returned only reviews; the single PDX-style pyrotinib hit the checker found (10.1002/ctm2.148) is gastric.

THYME (NCT00900627, HER2-low, paclitaxel with or without AZD8931, results 2014-09-29): a patient result for the existing azd8931-her2-low-xenograft-panel track, not a new system; belongs in the main draft.
Kim 2018 poziotinib phase 1 (10.4143/crt.2017.303) and Tjulandin 2014 AZD8931 phase 1 (10.1007/s10637-013-9963-6): human MTD/PK sources for the existing tracks B and A, not model systems.
Regulator reliance: no FDA/EMA review exists for any member (manifest has no rows; pyrotinib's NMPA review is not public), so no label-expansion-on-model-data case to score.
Human challenge, human genetic and ex-vivo drug-sensitivity systems: none found for pan-HER TKIs in breast cancer.
Hickinson 2010's HER2-non-overexpressing LoVo, FaDu and PC-9 xenografts: same system as the draft's track A.
